tagline.text: A pair of 40 m bamboo hanging bridges side by side over a river

location.label: Location
location.text: Over the Sipatan River linking Barangays Ewon and Lobgob in Sevilla, beside the Loay Interior Road, about 30–36 km from Tagbilaran

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: 1–2 hours (about 30 minutes as a stop on an inland Bohol tour)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱200~1,000 (per person, based on public transport from Tagbilaran or joining a tour, including the entrance fee)

children.text: The Sipatan Twin Hanging Bridge is a pair of bamboo hanging bridges side by side over a river, where you cross on one and return on the other. It is a popular stop on inland Bohol tours, the fee is about ₱20~50, and crossing takes only a few minutes.

The Sipatan Twin Hanging Bridge is a pair of hanging bridges side by side over the Sipatan River in Sevilla, inland Bohol. It is also called the Sevilla Twin Hanging Bridge, the Tigbao Hanging Bridge and the Bamboo Hanging Bridge. One source says it links Sitio Sipatan in Barangay Ewon with Sitio Llawod in Barangay Lobgob, while some guides place it in Loboc. You cross on one bridge and return on the other, which is why it is called a "twin" bridge. Each bridge is about
long with a deck of woven bamboo, so it sways and bounces with every step. One visitor puts the height above the ground at about

. It began after World War II as a bamboo-and-rope footbridge built by residents to carry farm produce and livestock across the river; the ropes have since been replaced by steel cables while the bamboo deck was kept.
In a travel plan this is a short stop. Crossing takes
2–3 minutes

even at a slow walk, and half an hour is enough even with photos and a snack on the far side. That is why most visitors include it as a midway stop on a one-day inland Bohol tour that covers the Bilar Man-Made Forest, the Loboc River cruise and the Chocolate Hills. One source says many tour vans stop here between the Bilar man-made forest and the Loboc River cruise, and another account describes a self-drive visit after Ingkumhan Falls and Dimiao Twin Falls. One reviewer wrote that the bridge looked unsafe at first sight but felt safe in the end, that locals still cross it, and that small motorcycles sometimes do too. Because the bridge is a daily route for residents, some guides say it is open 24 hours and charges only during the day.
Sevilla is a small town about
30 km

from Tagbilaran. The 2024 census counted about 11,000 residents; it covers about 64.55 sq km in 13 barangays and borders Balilihan, Bilar, Sikatuna and Loboc. A fiesta honoring its patron, Our Lady of Guadalupe, is held on December 12. The town is more a place you pass through on an inland Bohol drive, so follow the signs slowly to the entrance of the bridge. The surroundings are rice paddies and coconut groves, with limestone hills visible to the north. The average temperature is about
and annual rainfall is reported at about 1,395 mm, with April the driest month and November the wettest.

The bridge was reportedly destroyed by strong currents during Super Typhoon Odette in December 2021 and later rebuilt and reopened. So the present bridge may differ a little from the photos in older reviews. After the rebuild a provincial advisory was reported to charge ₱50 per person for guests aged 10 and over, but other sources give ₱20 or ₱35, so the differences between sources are large. The fee is explained as going toward upkeep of the bridge and barangay programs. Check the latest fee and opening hours locally before you visit. One guide also presents the bridge as a stop on the way to the Chocolate Hills, and says many travelers combine it with the Hinagdanan Cave, the Blood Compact Shrine, Mag-Aso Falls, the Bohol Bee Farm, Baclayon Church and the Loboc Wildlife and Nature Park.

You cross on one of the two parallel hanging bridges and return on the other, each carrying one direction of traffic. The bridge sways less when fewer people are on it, and if you are nervous you can let others go first.

blocks.title: The river seen from the bridge

children.text: The bridge hangs about
over a river in inland Bohol, and below you the river and forest are in view. In places you can see through the gaps in the bamboo, so if heights make you uneasy, hold the railing and walk slowly.

blocks.title: Rest area on the far side

children.text: On the far bank a multipurpose hall serves as a craft display and rest area. Stalls reportedly sell handicrafts, rice cakes and cold drinks. One reviewer in 2016 found some souvenir shops closed. There are also shops selling coconuts and snacks, and souvenirs such as T-shirts, bags, key chains and bracelets and Bohol delicacies are mentioned.

It was originally a bamboo-and-rope bridge that villagers used after World War II to move farm produce and livestock. The ropes were replaced by steel cables, and the deck of woven bamboo slats remains, so the floor bounces underfoot. One account says it was reinforced with a PACAP grant. Check locally for the structure after the rebuild.
From 8 to 10 a.m. the light is good and tour groups are fewer. In the afternoon tour vehicles increase, so arrive early if you want to take photos at leisure.
Busai Falls, reached by pump boat from the Sevilla–Loboc boundary up to Barangay Ewon, is described as quieter than the bridge. If you have time, ask locally about boats.
It is said to be about
10 minutes
by car from the bridge to Loboc and about
15–20 minutes
to the Chocolate Hills complex in Carmen. It is a good location for saving time on a tour.

The parish church and plaza of Sevilla are described as having Spanish-era origins, and the present building is said to be a later reconstruction. After the bridge it is nice to walk around town briefly.
See the Bilar Man-Made Forest and then move toward the bridge.
Pay the fee at the entrance and cross on one bridge.
Take photos in the rest area on the far side and buy a snack.
Return on the other bridge.
Move on toward the Loboc River cruise.
Aim for 8–10 a.m. to avoid large tour groups.
Leave Tagbilaran and see one or two waterfalls first.
Some itineraries first stop at Ingkumhan Falls or Dimiao Twin Falls.
Cross the Sipatan hanging bridge.
Have lunch in Loboc.
Combining the waterfalls and the bridge makes the driving distance longer. If you rent a car or motorcycle, check road conditions and return before dark.
Flights run from Manila to Bohol-Panglao International Airport (TAG) and take about
1 hour 20 minutes
. Check airlines and schedules when you book.
From the airport to Tagbilaran takes about
30 minutes
by taxi or van.
It is a stop on most inland Bohol tours. Booking a tour from your hotel in Panglao or Tagbilaran is convenient.
With a chartered vehicle you can change the order of the Bilar Man-Made Forest, the Loboc River and the Chocolate Hills to save time.
It is about
from Tagbilaran. Follow the national road toward Carmen or the Loay Interior Road; just before Loboc town there is said to be a short signed turnoff.

You can reportedly go by bus from Tagbilaran city proper, or by motorcycle, habal-habal or tricycle. One travel account says you can rent a motorcycle through your accommodation, but rates vary over time, so check. We could not confirm bus and jeepney fares and times, so check locally.
The bamboo deck gets slippery when wet, so the dry season is safer. In the rainy season the river can rise and use of the bridge may be restricted.
From 8 to 10 a.m. the light is good and there are few people, while tour groups crowd in during the afternoon.
Annual rainfall is reported at about 1,395 mm, with November the wettest month and April the driest. In the rainy season, check the river level and the condition of the deck locally.

There is reportedly almost no lodging around the bridge. One source says Sevilla has no accommodation yet lists a waterfall resort, so check recent reviews on a booking site. Most people come as a day trip from Tagbilaran or Panglao, and there are small guesthouses in Loboc and Bilar.

At the stalls on the far side of the bridge you can buy rice cakes and cold drinks. Lunch is typically the Loboc River cruise buffet or a restaurant in Loboc town. A common plan is to move toward Loboc, eat, and continue with the river scenery. Shops around the bridge sell coconuts, snacks, drinks and souvenirs. Because the bridge is close to the Loboc River cruise, it is easy to have lunch on the same route.
The bamboo deck is slippery, so wear closed shoes with firm soles.
Aim for 8–10 a.m. to avoid large tour groups. By day it is said to be crowded with both locals and foreign tourists.
Pay the fee in cash, so have small change ready.
When many people climb on at once the bridge sways a lot, so cross with spacing between you.
Cross on one bridge and return on the other, keeping to the direction of traffic.
Put a strap on your phone while taking photos so it does not fall.
Souvenirs at the stalls on the far side are said to be cheaper than in the city.
Stops on a tour are short, so decide your order of crossing in advance.
Some guides say the bridge is open 24 hours but the fee is charged by day, so if you cross early in the morning or at night, follow residents' guidance.
Stopping to take photos while crossing can endanger the people behind you, so take photos from the far bank.
The bridge has a swaying bamboo deck over a river, so do not push yourself if heights frighten you. Children must hold a guardian's hand when crossing.
The fee varies by source between ₱20 and ₱50, so check locally.
The bridge may be closed on rainy days or when the water is high.
It was reportedly rebuilt after the 2021 typhoon, so it may look different from older reviews.
Opening hours differ by source, from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. in some and 24 hours in others, so check locally.
The information in this article reflects what could be verified as of 2026; check the latest announcements.
The
Bilar Man-Made Forest
, the stop most often paired on tours, has giant mahogany trees forming a tunnel.
About 10 minutes by car from the bridge, a lunch cruise on the
Loboc River
is a standard stop.
The
Chocolate Hills
in Carmen are about 15–20 minutes by car.
Loboc Church
is a heritage site that fits easily into the same route.
Alona Beach
, which many day tours continue to in the afternoon, is Panglao's signature beach.
